/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: National Folk Museum of Korea + National Palace Museum of Korea both INSIDE Gyeongbokgung grounds (separate free admission). Cafes, restrooms, gift shop near entrance.

/itineraryStops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: Gyeongbokgung is Seoul's #1 must-see and the natural opener for any first-day-in-Seoul itinerary. Picked over Deoksugung (the smaller Western-influenced palace) because the changing-of-the-guard pageantry, the scale of the throne-hall complex, and the photogenic Gyeonghoeru/Hyangwonjeong pavilions deliver a single 90-min visit that explains 500 years of Joseon court life in concrete visual terms — essential for cruise passengers with one day in Korea. For cruise guests, the 90-min Gyeongbokgung dwell is also the day's primary deep-history anchor — first-time Korea visitors leave with a concrete visual framework (palace scale + ceremony pageantry + photogenic pavilions) that contextualizes every other Joseon-era reference in the country.

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/parking.source_en: Limited; tour bus drop-off zones at Gwanghwamun

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/restroom.source_en: At main entrance, mid-grounds, and rear pavilion area

/itineraryStops/1/description.source_en:
Gyeongbokgung — meaning 'Palace Greatly Blessed by Heaven' — was the main royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty, built 1395 (3rd year of King Taejo's reign) as the heart of the new capital Hanyang (now Seoul). It is the largest of the Five Grand Palaces of Joseon and once contained 330+ buildings serviced by 3,000 staff. 

Burned during the 1592 Imjin War, the palace lay in ruins for 273 years until King Gojong rebuilt it in 1867; the Japanese colonial administration demolished much of the rebuilt complex 1910-1945, and the painstaking restoration that began in 1990 continues today. Three centerpieces define the visit: **Geunjeongjeon Throne Hall** — the largest wooden building in Korea, where kings held court and received foreign envoys; **Gyeonghoeru Pavilion** — a two-story pavilion on 48 stone pillars over a lotus pond, used for royal banquets; and **Hyangwonjeong Pavilion** — a hexagonal pavilion on a small island reached by a covered bridge, considered Korea's most photographed garden scene. 

The **Royal Guard Changing Ceremony** takes place daily at 10:00 and 14:00 (approximately 20 min) — guards in vivid blue, red, and yellow Joseon-era uniforms with traditional drums and horns recreate the historic palace gate-protection ritual. 

**Critical scheduling note**: Gyeongbokgung is CLOSED ON TUESDAYS — when this falls, the tour substitutes Changdeokgung Palace, the only Korean palace inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage (1997), which is closed Mondays instead. 

Visitors wearing hanbok (traditional Korean dress, rentable nearby in Bukchon for ~15,000 KRW/4hr) enter the palace FREE — a popular photo-trip combination.

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Mar-May, Sep-Oct: 09:00-18:00; Jun-Aug: 09:00-18:30; Nov-Feb: 09:00-17:00 (last admission 1 hr before close)

/itineraryStops/1/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Adult 3,000 KRW / Child 1,500 KRW; FREE for hanbok-wearers; Integrated Palace Ticket 6,000 KRW (4 palaces + Jongmyo, valid for 6 months; excludes Changdeokgung Secret Garden)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/0.source_en: Seoul's largest preserved hanok district — ~900 traditional homes in a single compact area

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/1.source_en: Bukchon 8 Gyeong (8 famous viewpoints) — the iconic hanok-roofline-with-N-Seoul-Tower view at #6

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/2.source_en: Live residential village (not a museum) — residents request quiet hours and respectful behavior

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/3.source_en: Cultural workshops: Korean knot-tying, hanji paper crafts, tea ceremony, embroidery

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/4.source_en: Hanbok rental shops at village edge for free Gyeongbokgung admission combo

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/6.source_en: **~600 years old** — historic district between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung Palaces, originally home to Joseon Dynasty high-ranking officials and aristocracy

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/7.source_en: **Red Zone entry restriction 17:00–10:00 enforced** — village is a LIVING residential community (not a museum); cultural respect protocol critical (no flash photography in alleys, voices down, no drones)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/8.source_en: **Integrated Palace Ticket ₩6,000 adult** covers the 4 main palaces + Jongmyo Shrine for 6 months; Changdeokgung Secret Garden is a separate ticket.

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/tip.source_en: **Visit before noon or after 16:00** — residents have publicly requested quieter visits; some lanes have signs prohibiting tour groups during early-morning resident hours. Stay quiet and on the marked photo paths. Hanbok rental shops at the village edge — Hanboknam, Oneday Hanbok, etc. Combine with ⟦G0⟧ (5 min walk) and Gyeongbokgung (10 min walk) for a Seoul-northside half-day.
